correctness.rationale: The frozen six-file Git tree was independently reconstructed from the real blob SHAs and matched the assigned source SHA. The nonstandard input is Denčić--Stanković--Krstić--Damnjanović Theorem 2.1, examined in its full proof, which gives omega_r(A)=(||A||/2)[1+r c+sqrt(1-r^2)sqrt(1-c^2)] for rank-one A, c=|tr A|/||A|| in [0,1]. For complex q the scaled q-range is phase invariant, so Omega_q(A) contained in the closed disk iff omega_r(A)<=r. Rearranging gives the stated pointwise inequality for ||A||. For each 0<r<1, g(c)=rc+s sqrt(1-c^2) has g''(c)=-s(1-c^2)^(-3/2)<0 on (0,1), so its minima are exactly endpoints c=0 or c=1; when s=r the endpoints tie and no interior c minimizes. For r=1, g(c)=c, so c=0 is uniquely minimizing. Every c in [0,1] is realized by a rank-one operator on complex H of dimension>=2, using unit factors e1 and c e1+sqrt(1-c^2)e2. The equality condition c=1 gives a scalar multiple of an orthogonal rank-one projection by Cauchy--Schwarz; c=0 gives A^2=(tr A)A=0. The threshold r=s occurs only at 1/sqrt(2). The square-zero branch solves 2r/(1+sqrt(1-r^2))=1 exactly at r=4/5, and r=1 yields R1(1)=2. Strict inequalities and equality cases hold with r>0; no invalid r=0 division or claim about rank>=2 is made.

originality.rationale: The submitted rank-one scaled-disk envelope and both endpoint extremizer classes are mathematically contained in already published results. In particular, the complete published sharp two-sided rank-one comparison of q- and rho-numerical radii yields, on setting rho=1 (so omega_rho(T)=||T||), the exact sharp constant M_{1,r}=max{2/(1+sqrt(1-r^2)),2/(1+r)} for ||T||/omega_r(T). Because Omega_q(T) subset closed disk iff omega_r(T)<=r and positive scaling is unrestricted, the submitted supremum is exactly R_1(r)=r M_{1,r}. The comparison theorem proves endpoint maximizers: trace overlap zero (square-zero rank one) versus overlap one (scalar rank-one projection), switching exactly when r=sqrt(1-r^2), i.e. r=1/sqrt(2). Its q=1 boundary is included. Thus the whole sharp envelope, strict classifications and equality case are a direct rho=1 specialization, rather than new operator geometry; both relevant records have public date 2026-10-11 so no finer same-day chronological priority is asserted. Independently and earlier (2025-03-06), Denčić et al. Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.3 establish the exact normalized q-radius for every rank-one T: omega_r(T)/||T||=(1+r c+sqrt(1-r^2)sqrt(1-c^2))/2. Minimizing the final concave term on c in [0,1] immediately gives the same two endpoints, with all equality cases. The 2026 universal scaled q-spectral theorem supplies the separate coefficient rho_q=max{1,2r/(1+sqrt(1-r^2))}; the submitted 4/5 comparison is solving an elementary scalar equality using already established constants. No exact printed phrase need match: the full mathematical claim is covered by stronger published statements.
residual_risks: The two same-day 2026-10-11 published findings have no established within-day priority; the conclusion is mathematical coverage rather than an allegation of copying or chronological precedence.

value.rationale: The constrained norm bound for nonzero rank-one operators is a natural, motivated operator-theoretic observable, and the projection/nilpotent switch is an interpretable parameter boundary. Nevertheless this submission does not determine an independently unknown exact invariant: the complete rank-one operator norm/q-radius comparison with the same equality classes is already a published rho=1 specialization of a two-parameter theorem, and even the older 2025 exact normalized formula reduces the work to a two-endpoint concavity check. The only extra 4/5 observation equates a branch of that known ratio with a known universal coefficient. No new structural lemma, motivated counterexample beyond the already covered extremizers, or uncovered classification remains. This is a useful worked corollary, not a new mathematically valuable result under the stated nontriviality bar.
residual_risks: A special-case exposition can retain pedagogical utility; this FAIL refers to independent new mathematical value, not to the usefulness of the formula in applications.
The value judgment rests on explicit coverage and elementary implications, not merely on the short proof or lack of a downstream theorem.
